name: Jonatan Söderström
milestone_by_age_26: Won the IGF Nuovo Award at GDC 2010 at age 24 for his experimental puzzle game Tuning, after receiving two IGF nominations in 2008 for Clean Asia!; had developed over 40 freeware games by this point, establishing himself as a cult legend in indie circles.
starting_point: Born in 1985 in Sweden; developed games using Game Maker from a young age as a solo freeware developer.
current_position: Independent game developer based in Gothenburg, Sweden; co-founder of Dennaton Games, best known for the Hotline Miami series.

trajectory.title: Began freeware game development
trajectory.description: Started creating experimental freeware games under the alias 'Cactus,' quickly becoming one of the most prolific and influential developers in the Game Maker community.

trajectory.title: IGF nominations for Clean Asia!
trajectory.description: Received two Independent Games Festival nominations for Excellence in Visual Arts and Excellence in Audio for his 2D space shooter Clean Asia!.

trajectory.title: GDC talk and IndieCade award
trajectory.description: Delivered 'The Four-Hour Game Design' talk at GDC 2009 and won the Sublime Experience award at IndieCade for his puzzle game Tuning.

trajectory.title: Won IGF Nuovo Award
trajectory.description: Won the IGF Nuovo Award at GDC 2010 for Tuning, honoring unconventional and experimental game design, after having developed over 40 freeware titles.

trajectory.title: Released Hotline Miami
trajectory.description: Co-designed and programmed Hotline Miami with Dennis Wedin, published by Devolver Digital; the game became a cult hit praised for its brutal gameplay and surreal aesthetic.

trajectory.title: Released Hotline Miami 2
trajectory.description: Released Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number, the sequel to Hotline Miami, concluding the series and cementing his legacy in indie gaming.

trajectory.title: Uurnog Uurnlimited
trajectory.description: Released Uurnog: Uurnlimited, an experimental puzzle-platformer published by Nifflas, continuing his tradition of unconventional game design.

name: Davey Wreden
milestone_by_age_26: Released The Stanley Parable mod for Half-Life 2 on July 31, 2011 at age 22, which went viral online; later co-created the standalone remake released October 17, 2013 at age 25, which received critical acclaim and BAFTA nominations.
starting_point: Born in 1988 in Austin, Texas; attended University of Southern California's film school before turning to game design.
current_position: Game designer and co-founder of Ivy Road studio; released Wanderstop in 2025; lives in Vancouver, BC.

trajectory.title: Began game development
trajectory.description: Started developing video games, inspired by the Dear Esther mod to try his hand at modding Valve's Source Engine.

trajectory.title: Released The Stanley Parable mod
trajectory.description: Released The Stanley Parable as a free mod for Half-Life 2 on July 31, 2011, which went viral online for its innovative approach to player agency and narrative.

trajectory.title: Stanley Parable standalone release
trajectory.description: Co-created the standalone remake of The Stanley Parable with William Pugh, released October 17, 2013; it sold 50,000 copies on the first day and received critical acclaim and BAFTA nominations.

trajectory.title: Released The Beginner's Guide
trajectory.description: Released The Beginner's Guide, a narrative-driven game exploring creative struggles and authorship, which received widespread critical acclaim.

trajectory.title: Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe
trajectory.description: Collaborated with CrowsCrowsCrows to release The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, an expanded version for modern consoles.

trajectory.title: Released Wanderstop
trajectory.description: Released Wanderstop through his new studio Ivy Road, a contemplative narrative game about a former athlete running a tea shop.

name: Derek Yu
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created Aquaria, which won the IGF Seumas McNally Grand Prize ($20,000) in March 2007 at age 24; released the highly influential Spelunky as freeware in December 2008 at age 26.
starting_point: Born in 1982 in the United States; exposed to computer games via an Atari 2600 as a child; graduated from UC Berkeley with a degree in computer science.
current_position: Independent game designer, artist, and blogger; runs Mossmouth and the influential TIGSource indie game community; creator of Spelunky.

trajectory.title: Released Eternal Daughter
trajectory.description: Created the mega old-school platformer Eternal Daughter as freeware, described by 1up.com as a 'must-play bit of freeware.'

trajectory.title: Won IGF Grand Prize for Aquaria
trajectory.description: Co-created Aquaria with Alec Holowka through their company Bit Blot, winning the Seumas McNally Grand Prize ($20,000) at the 2007 IGF.

trajectory.title: Released Spelunky freeware
trajectory.description: Released the original Spelunky as freeware in December 2008, a roguelike platformer that would become one of the most influential indie games of all time.

trajectory.title: Spelunky HD release
trajectory.description: Released the remade Spelunky on Xbox Live Arcade, published by Microsoft, which became a critical and commercial success and defined the roguelike-platformer genre.

trajectory.title: Released Spelunky 2
trajectory.description: Released Spelunky 2, the highly anticipated sequel, which deepened the original's mechanics and was widely acclaimed.

name: Asher Vollmer
milestone_by_age_26: Released Threes on February 6, 2014 at age 24, which won Apple Game of the Year 2014 and the Apple Design Award 2014, and received an IGF Excellence in Design honorable mention.
starting_point: Born in 1989 in Los Angeles; father was a software engineer; attended USC Interactive Media & Games Division program.
current_position: Independent game developer; worked on Guildlings and other projects through Sirvo Studios.

trajectory.title: Released Puzzlejuice
trajectory.description: Released Puzzlejuice, an iOS puzzle game combining Tetris and word games, developed with artist Greg Wohlwend while a student at USC.

trajectory.title: Joined thatgamecompany
trajectory.description: Started as thatgamecompany's 'feel engineer' in August 2012, but left in April 2013 to go indie.

trajectory.title: Released Threes
trajectory.description: Released Threes on February 6, 2014, a puzzle game that won Apple Game of the Year 2014, the Apple Design Award, and an IGF Excellence in Design honorable mention.

trajectory.title: Worked on Close Castles and Royals
trajectory.description: Developed Close Castles (a real-time strategy game later put on hiatus) and Royals, a simulation game for macOS and Windows.

trajectory.title: Released Guildlings
trajectory.description: Released Guildlings through Sirvo Studios, an adventure RPG for mobile devices.

name: Gabriele Cirulli
milestone_by_age_26: Created 2048 on March 9, 2014 at age 19, a browser-based puzzle game that went viral with over 10 million unique visitors and 100 million plays within weeks of release.
starting_point: Born in Italy circa 1995; graduated high school in 2013; self-taught web developer who did not attend university.
current_position: UX/UI designer and developer; creator and owner of 2048; previously worked at 1Password and Impraise; runs play2048.co full-time.

trajectory.title: Created 2048
trajectory.description: Built 2048 in a weekend in March 2014 as an open-source browser puzzle game inspired by 1024 and Threes; it went viral on Hacker News with over 10 million unique visitors and 100 million plays within weeks.

trajectory.title: Joined Impraise via YC
trajectory.description: Joined Impraise, a YCombinator Summer 2014 startup, as a UX/UI designer and developer, working there for three years.

trajectory.title: Moved to WodUp
trajectory.description: Worked as a UX/UI designer and developer at WodUp, designing software for CrossFit gyms and athletes.

trajectory.title: Joined 1Password
trajectory.description: Worked as a designer and developer at 1Password for nearly four years, helping bring their apps to the next level.

trajectory.title: Rebuilt 2048 full-time
trajectory.description: Quit his job to work on 2048 full-time, building a completely new version of the game for its 10th anniversary in 2024.

trajectory.title: Launched new 2048
trajectory.description: Released a completely rewritten version of 2048 as a tribute to the original, now hosted on play2048.co.

name: William Pugh
milestone_by_age_26: Co-created The Stanley Parable standalone game released October 17, 2013 at approximately age 18-19, which received critical acclaim and three BAFTA nominations; named BAFTA Breakthrough Brit in 2014 at age 19-20.
starting_point: Born in 1994/1995 in the UK; son of two art teachers; fell in love with video games during a hospital visit at age six; briefly attended Leeds College of Art.
current_position: Founder of Crows Crows Crows, an indie game studio in London; game designer and creative director.

trajectory.title: Began modding Valve games
trajectory.description: Taught himself video game environment design by creating mods for Team Fortress 2, Left 4 Dead 2, and Portal, eventually winning a Saxxy Award for his TF2 creations.

trajectory.title: Co-created The Stanley Parable
trajectory.description: Collaborated remotely with Davey Wreden for two years to release the standalone Stanley Parable in October 2013, which became a critical and commercial hit.

trajectory.title: Named BAFTA Breakthrough Brit
trajectory.description: Named a BAFTA Breakthrough Brit in 2014 and received the IGF Audience Award for The Stanley Parable.

trajectory.title: Founded Crows Crows Crows
trajectory.description: Founded the indie game studio Crows Crows Crows, funneling earnings from The Stanley Parable into producing experimental games with a team of contractors.

trajectory.title: Released Dr. Langeskov
trajectory.description: Released 'Dr. Langeskov, The Tiger and The Terribly Cursed Emerald: A Whirlwind Heist,' a free experimental narrative game.

trajectory.title: Released Accounting+
trajectory.description: Released Accounting+, a VR comedy game, in collaboration with Justin Roiland.

trajectory.title: The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe
trajectory.description: Co-released The Stanley Parable: Ultra Deluxe, an expanded version of the original game for modern platforms.

name: Joey King
milestone_by_age_26: Nominated for the Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actress in a Limited Series or Movie for The Act (2019) at age 20, also receiving Golden Globe and SAG nominations for the same role.
starting_point: Born July 30, 1999 in Los Angeles; began acting professionally at age four in a Life Cereal commercial; sister of actress Hunter King.
current_position: Actress and producer; married to Steven Piet; starred in films including Bullet Train and A Family Affair; active in both acting and producing.

trajectory.title: Film debut in Reign Over Me
trajectory.description: Made her film debut in Reign Over Me (2007), beginning a prolific child acting career.

trajectory.title: Lead role in Ramona and Beezus
trajectory.description: Starred as Ramona Quimby in Ramona and Beezus, her first lead role in a feature film, winning a Young Artist Award.

trajectory.title: The Dark Knight Rises
trajectory.description: Appeared in Christopher Nolan's The Dark Knight Rises, followed by roles in The Conjuring and Oz the Great and Powerful in 2013.

trajectory.title: The Kissing Booth breakout
trajectory.description: Starred in The Kissing Booth on Netflix, which became a massive hit and spawned a trilogy through 2021, catapulting her to widespread fame.

trajectory.title: Emmy nomination for The Act
trajectory.description: Received Primetime Emmy, Golden Globe, and SAG nominations for her critically acclaimed portrayal of Gypsy-Rose Blanchard in The Act (2019).

trajectory.title: Bullet Train and The Princess
trajectory.description: Starred in lead action roles in Bullet Train (with Brad Pitt) and The Princess, expanding into action cinema.

trajectory.title: A Family Affair and Despicable Me 4
trajectory.description: Starred in the romantic comedy A Family Affair with Nicole Kidman and voiced a character in Despicable Me 4.

name: Marsai Martin
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest Hollywood executive producer in history at age 14 for the film Little (2019), holding a Guinness World Record, while also starring in the film and maintaining her role on ABC's Black-ish since age 10.
starting_point: Born August 14, 2004 in Plano, Texas; parents Carol and Joshua Martin; family moved to Los Angeles in 2013 to pursue her acting career.
current_position: Actress and producer; founder of Genius Entertainment; starred in and produced G20 (2025); continues acting and producing at age 21.

trajectory.title: Cast in Black-ish
trajectory.description: Cast as Diane Johnson on the ABC sitcom Black-ish, a breakout role that earned her three NAACP Image Awards and multiple SAG nominations.

trajectory.title: Youngest Hollywood executive producer
trajectory.description: Produced and starred in the film Little at age 14, earning a Guinness World Record as the youngest Hollywood executive producer; the film grossed $48M globally.

trajectory.title: Time 100 Next and first-look deal
trajectory.description: Named to Time's 'Time 100 Next' list and became the youngest person to sign a first-look deal at a studio.

trajectory.title: Fantasy Football and Saturdays
trajectory.description: Produced and starred in Fantasy Football on Paramount+ and executive produced the Disney Channel comedy Saturdays.

trajectory.title: Starred in G20
trajectory.description: Starred in and produced the action thriller G20, continuing her transition from child star to Hollywood mogul through Genius Entertainment.

name: Thomasin McKenzie
milestone_by_age_26: Rose to critical prominence with the lead role in Debra Granik's Leave No Trace (2018) at age 18, winning the National Board of Review Award for Breakthrough Performance, followed by a key role in the Oscar-nominated Jojo Rabbit (2019) at age 19.
starting_point: Born July 26, 2000 in Wellington, New Zealand; daughter of actress Miranda Harcourt and director Stuart McKenzie; granddaughter of actress Dame Kate Harcourt.
current_position: Actress; starred in Eileen (2023), Joy (2024), and The Testament of Ann Lee (2025); one of New Zealand's leading international film actresses.

trajectory.title: Early film appearance in Existence
trajectory.description: Appeared with her brother in the film Existence, beginning her acting career in New Zealand.

trajectory.title: Role in The Hobbit
trajectory.description: Had a minor role in The Hobbit: The Battle of the Five Armies, followed by roles in New Zealand television including Shortland Street.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough in Leave No Trace
trajectory.description: Rose to critical prominence with the lead role in Debra Granik's Leave No Trace, winning the National Board of Review Award for Breakthrough Performance.

trajectory.title: Jojo Rabbit and The King
trajectory.description: Played the Jewish girl Elsa Korr in the Oscar-nominated Jojo Rabbit and appeared in The King with Timothee Chalamet.

trajectory.title: Last Night in Soho and Power of the Dog
trajectory.description: Starred in Edgar Wright's Last Night in Soho and appeared in Jane Campion's Oscar-nominated The Power of the Dog, establishing herself as a leading actress.

trajectory.title: Lead role in Eileen
trajectory.description: Played the title role in the thriller Eileen, an adaptation of the Ottessa Moshfegh novel.

trajectory.title: Joy and continued prolific output
trajectory.description: Played embryologist Jean Purdy in the biographical drama Joy about the birth of IVF.

name: Markus Villig
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Bolt (then Taxify) at age 19 in 2013, and by age 25 in 2019 it became Europe's youngest unicorn, making him Europe's youngest founder of a billion-dollar company.
starting_point: Born December 17, 1993 on Saaremaa, Estonia; father had a computing degree from University of Moscow, mother was a professor; brother worked at Skype.
current_position: Founder and CEO of Bolt; Europe's youngest self-made billionaire; board member of Klarna; based in Tallinn, Estonia.

trajectory.title: Founded Bolt (Taxify)
trajectory.description: Launched Bolt (then Taxify) with a EUR 5,000 loan from his family after graduating high school, personally recruiting taxi drivers on the streets of Tallinn.

trajectory.title: Dropped out of university
trajectory.description: Left the University of Tartu after one semester of computer science to work on Bolt full-time.

trajectory.title: Forbes 30 Under 30
trajectory.description: Featured as the youngest CEO on the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in the Baltics and received Estonia's presidential award for Best Young Entrepreneur.

trajectory.title: DiDi Chuxing investment
trajectory.description: Secured investment from China's DiDi Chuxing, bringing capital and credibility to Bolt's expansion across Europe and Africa.

trajectory.title: Europe's youngest unicorn founder
trajectory.description: Bolt became Europe's youngest unicorn, making Villig the youngest founder of a billion-dollar company in Europe.

trajectory.title: Self-made billionaire
trajectory.description: Following Bolt's $8.4 billion valuation fundraise, Villig became Europe's youngest self-made billionaire.

trajectory.title: Klarna board member
trajectory.description: Appointed as a board member of Klarna, expanding his influence in the European fintech ecosystem.

name: Neymar da Silva Santos Júnior
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Copa Libertadores with Santos FC in 2011 at age 19 and was named South American Footballer of the Year in both 2011 and 2012, before transferring to Barcelona for ~£49M in 2013 and winning the Champions League treble in 2014-15.
starting_point: Born February 5, 1992 in Mogi das Cruzes, Sao Paulo, Brazil; son of a former professional footballer; joined Santos youth academy at age 11.
current_position: Playing for Santos FC (returned January 2025); previously at Al-Hilal, PSG, and Barcelona; Brazil's all-time top international scorer; net worth estimated ~$250M.

trajectory.title: Professional debut at Santos
trajectory.description: Made his professional debut for Santos FC and won the Best Young Player award in the Brazilian league.

trajectory.title: Copa Libertadores and Puskas Award
trajectory.description: Won the Copa Libertadores with Santos, was named South American Footballer of the Year, and won the FIFA Puskas Award for goal of the year.

trajectory.title: Transfer to Barcelona
trajectory.description: Transferred to FC Barcelona for approximately GBP 49M, becoming one of the most expensive transfers at the time.

trajectory.title: Champions League treble
trajectory.description: Won the treble (La Liga, Copa del Rey, Champions League) with Barcelona, scoring 39 goals in all competitions including in the Champions League final.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold with Brazil
trajectory.description: Led Brazil to its first Olympic gold medal at the Rio 2016 Olympics, scoring the winning penalty in the final.

trajectory.title: World record transfer to PSG
trajectory.description: Joined Paris Saint-Germain for a world-record EUR 222M, becoming the most expensive player in football history.

trajectory.title: Move to Al-Hilal
trajectory.description: Transferred to Saudi club Al-Hilal, before returning to Santos FC in January 2025.

name: Benito Antonio Martínez Ocasio (Bad Bunny)
milestone_by_age_26: Rose to prominence in 2016 at age 22 with 'Diles' on SoundCloud, signed with Hear This Music, released hit 'Soy Peor' in 2016, and dropped debut album 'X 100pre' on Dec 31, 2018 at age 24, which was ranked among Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.
starting_point: Born March 10, 1994 in Bayamon, Puerto Rico; studied audiovisual communication at University of Puerto Rico at Arecibo; worked as a grocery store bagger while making music.
current_position: One of the world's biggest music artists; six-time Grammy winner; headlined Super Bowl LX halftime show in 2026; first Spanish-language artist to win Grammy Album of the Year.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough with 'Diles'
trajectory.description: Rose to prominence on SoundCloud with 'Diles,' leading to a recording contract with Hear This Music; released hit 'Soy Peor' in December 2016.

trajectory.title: Debut album X 100pre
trajectory.description: Released debut album 'X 100pre' on December 31, 2018, which debuted at #11 on the Billboard 200 and was ranked among Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Albums of All Time.

trajectory.title: Oasis collaboration and 'I Like It'
trajectory.description: Released collaborative album Oasis with J Balvin and scored a Billboard Hot 100 #1 with 'I Like It' (with Cardi B and J Balvin).

trajectory.title: YHLQMDLG and El Ultimo Tour del Mundo
trajectory.description: Released YHLQMDLG, Spotify's most-streamed album of the year, and El Ultimo Tour del Mundo, the first all-Spanish album to top the Billboard 200.

trajectory.title: Un Verano Sin Ti
trajectory.description: Released Un Verano Sin Ti, the year's most successful album globally, which was nominated for Grammy Album of the Year.

trajectory.title: Grammy Album of the Year
trajectory.description: Won the Grammy Award for Album of the Year for 'Debi Tirar Mas Fotos,' the first Spanish-language album to win the award.

trajectory.title: Super Bowl halftime show
trajectory.description: Headlined the Super Bowl LX halftime show to great acclaim and controversy, cementing his status as a global pop icon.

name: Carolina Giraldo Navarro (Karol G)
milestone_by_age_26: Signed with Universal Music Latino in 2016 at age 25 and released singles including 'Casi Nada' (15M+ YouTube views) and 'Hello' with Ozuna, performing at Premios Juventud before her breakthrough hit 'Ahora Me Llama' with Bad Bunny in May 2017.
starting_point: Born February 14, 1991 in Medellin, Colombia; father Guillermo Giraldo was a musician; appeared on Colombian X Factor at age 14; moved to New York in 2014.
current_position: One of the world's leading Latin music artists; Grammy winner; first woman to debut at #1 on Billboard 200 with a Spanish-language album; based in Colombia.

trajectory.title: First single and early career
trajectory.description: Released her first single at age 16 and spent the next decade struggling to establish herself in the male-dominated reggaeton genre.

trajectory.title: Moved to New York
trajectory.description: Moved to New York to learn more about the music industry, eventually signing with Universal Music Latino in 2016.

trajectory.title: Debut album Unstoppable
trajectory.description: Released debut album 'Unstoppable' in October 2017, led by the breakthrough hit 'Ahora Me Llama' with Bad Bunny.

trajectory.title: 'Tusa' and Ocean album
trajectory.description: Released the album Ocean and the massive hit 'Tusa' with Nicki Minaj, which was certified 28x Latin platinum and charted internationally.

trajectory.title: Mañana Será Bonito makes history
trajectory.description: Released 'Manana Sera Bonito,' the first Spanish-language album by a female artist to debut at #1 on the US Billboard 200.

trajectory.title: Grammy Award win
trajectory.description: Won her first Grammy Award at the 66th annual ceremony for Best Musica Urbana Album, cementing her status as a global superstar.

name: Juan Luis Londoño Arias (Maluma)
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut album 'Magia' in 2012 at age 18 (nominated for Latin Grammy Best New Artist), followed by breakthrough album 'Pretty Boy, Dirty Boy' in 2015 which topped the Top Latin Albums chart, and became the first male Latino artist with 10M+ Instagram followers in 2016.
starting_point: Born January 28, 1994 in Medellin, Colombia; father worked at a logistics company, mother was a homemaker; played youth football before turning to music at 16.
current_position: Colombian singer, rapper, and actor; one of the best-selling Latin music artists with 18M+ records sold; based in Medellin.

trajectory.title: First single 'Farandulera'
trajectory.description: Recorded his first independent single 'Farandulera' at age 16, which gained internet popularity and radio airplay in Colombia.

trajectory.title: Debut album Magia
trajectory.description: Released debut album 'Magia' on Sony Music Colombia, which earned a Latin Grammy nomination for Best New Artist.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough with Pretty Boy, Dirty Boy
trajectory.description: Released 'Pretty Boy, Dirty Boy,' which topped the Billboard Top Latin Albums chart and launched him to mainstream Latin pop success.

trajectory.title: First male Latino with 10M Instagram followers
trajectory.description: Became the first male Latino artist to surpass 10 million followers on Instagram, cementing his social media dominance.

trajectory.title: F.A.M.E. and Latin Grammy
trajectory.description: Released F.A.M.E., which won the Latin Grammy for Best Contemporary Pop Vocal Album.

trajectory.title: Papi Juancho and 'Hawai'
trajectory.description: Released Papi Juancho with the hit 'Hawai,' which reached #3 on the Billboard Global 200 and #1 on the Global Excl. U.S. chart when remixed with The Weeknd.

trajectory.title: Marry Me film debut
trajectory.description: Starred alongside Jennifer Lopez in the romantic comedy Marry Me, making his Hollywood acting debut.

name: Juan Carlos Ozuna Rosado (Ozuna)
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut album 'Odisea' in September 2017 at age 25, which topped the Billboard Top Latin Albums chart for 46 weeks (second-longest run ever), debuted at #22 on the Billboard 200, and appeared 8 times simultaneously on the Hot Latin Songs chart.
starting_point: Born March 13, 1992 in San Juan, Puerto Rico; decided to become a singer at age 12; discovered by producer Fernando Acevedo in Santurce, Puerto Rico.
current_position: Puerto Rican reggaeton singer with five #1 Billboard Top Latin Albums; one of the most streamed Latin artists globally.

trajectory.title: Musical debut with 'Imaginando'
trajectory.description: Debuted as a singer with the song 'Imaginando,' beginning to build a following through online singles.

trajectory.title: Radio hits across Latin America
trajectory.description: Songs like 'Si Tu Marido No Te Quiere' became radio hits across Latin America, and he performed concerts in numerous countries.

trajectory.title: Breakthrough with 'La Ocasion'
trajectory.description: Joined DJ Luian, Mambo Kingz, and Anuel AA on 'La Ocasion,' which peaked in the Top 30 of Hot Latin Songs and launched his chart career.

trajectory.title: Debut album Odisea
trajectory.description: Released debut album 'Odisea' on August 25, 2017, which topped the Billboard Top Latin Albums chart for 46 weeks and debuted at #22 on the Billboard 200.

trajectory.title: Aura album and 'Taki Taki'
trajectory.description: Released second album 'Aura,' which debuted at #7 on the Billboard 200, and collaborated on the quadruple-platinum hit 'Taki Taki' with DJ Snake, Cardi B, and Selena Gomez.

trajectory.title: Nibiru album
trajectory.description: Released third studio album 'Nibiru,' continuing his streak of #1 Billboard Top Latin Albums.

name: Julio Yamel Rodríguez
milestone_by_age_26: Made MLB debut on April 8, 2022 at age 21, was named AL Rookie of the Year and All-Star in his rookie season, won the Silver Slugger Award, and signed a contract worth $210-470M with the Seattle Mariners.
starting_point: Born December 29, 2000 in Loma de Cabrera, Dominican Republic; signed with Seattle Mariners as an international free agent at age 16 for $1.75M.
current_position: Center fielder for the Seattle Mariners; 3x All-Star; signed to a contract worth up to $470M; one of MLB's biggest young stars.

trajectory.title: Signed with Mariners
trajectory.description: Signed as an international free agent with the Seattle Mariners at age 16 for a $1.75 million signing bonus in July 2017.

trajectory.title: Dominican Summer League MVP
trajectory.description: Named MVP of the Dominican Summer League in his professional debut season, batting .315 with 5 home runs and 10 stolen bases.

trajectory.title: Olympic appearance for DR
trajectory.description: Represented the Dominican Republic at the Tokyo Olympics, batting .462 with a 1.069 OPS and slugging a home run in the bronze medal game.

trajectory.title: MLB debut and Rookie of the Year
trajectory.description: Made MLB debut on April 8, 2022; named AL Rookie of the Year, All-Star, and Silver Slugger winner after hitting 28 home runs with 25 stolen bases.

trajectory.title: $210M contract extension
trajectory.description: Signed a long-term contract extension with the Mariners worth $210M that could max out at $470M, one of the largest deals in MLB history.

trajectory.title: All-MLB First Team
trajectory.description: Named to the All-MLB First Team in 2025, continuing his trajectory as one of baseball's premier outfielders.

name: Ronald Acuña Jr.
milestone_by_age_26: Made MLB debut on April 25, 2018 at age 20, won NL Rookie of the Year in 2018, became the youngest player in MLB history to hit 40+ home runs and steal 70+ bases in a single season (2023 at age 25), and was named NL MVP in 2023.
starting_point: Born December 18, 1997 in La Guaira, Venezuela; son of a former minor league baseball player; signed with Atlanta Braves for $100,000 as an international free agent in 2014.
current_position: Outfielder for the Atlanta Braves; NL MVP (2023); only player in MLB history with 40+ HR and 70+ SB in a single season; recovering from injury.

trajectory.title: Signed with Atlanta Braves
trajectory.description: Signed with the Atlanta Braves for $100,000 as an international free agent in July 2014.

trajectory.title: Top MLB prospect
trajectory.description: Ranked as the #1 MLB prospect by Baseball America heading into the 2018 season after dominating across multiple minor league levels.

trajectory.title: MLB debut and NL Rookie of the Year
trajectory.description: Made MLB debut on April 25, 2018, and won the National League Rookie of the Year Award after hitting 26 home runs with 16 stolen bases.

trajectory.title: All-Star and 40-40 chase
trajectory.description: Named an All-Star and hit 41 home runs with 37 stolen bases, narrowly missing a 40-40 season and winning his first Silver Slugger.

trajectory.title: Historic 40-70 season and NL MVP
trajectory.description: Became the first player in MLB history to hit 40+ home runs and steal 70+ bases in a single season, winning the NL MVP Award unanimously.

trajectory.title: ACL injury
trajectory.description: Suffered a torn ACL in May 2024, ending his season and requiring extensive rehabilitation.

name: Yordan Ruben Alvarez
milestone_by_age_26: Made MLB debut on June 9, 2019 at age 22 and was unanimously named AL Rookie of the Year after posting the highest slugging percentage (.655) by a qualified rookie in MLB history; later won the World Series with the Houston Astros in 2022 and was named ALCS MVP in 2021.
starting_point: Born June 27, 1997 in Las Tunas, Cuba; defected from Cuba in 2016 and established residency in Haiti; signed with the Los Angeles Dodgers before being traded to Houston.
current_position: Designated hitter and left fielder for the Houston Astros; 4x All-Star; World Series champion; one of MLB's most feared power hitters.

trajectory.title: Defected from Cuba and signed
trajectory.description: Defected from Cuba, established residency in Haiti, and signed with the Los Angeles Dodgers as an international free agent in June 2016.

trajectory.title: Traded to Houston Astros
trajectory.description: Was traded from the Dodgers to the Houston Astros in exchange for Josh Fields on August 1, 2016, before making his professional debut.

trajectory.title: MLB debut and unanimous AL Rookie of the Year
trajectory.description: Made his MLB debut on June 9, 2019, and was unanimously named AL Rookie of the Year after posting a .655 slugging percentage, the highest by a qualified rookie in MLB history.

trajectory.title: ALCS MVP
trajectory.description: Named ALCS MVP after a dominant postseason performance against the Boston Red Sox, hitting .522 with four home runs.

trajectory.title: World Series champion and All-Star
trajectory.description: Won the World Series with the Houston Astros, was named an All-Star for the first time, and won the Silver Slugger Award after hitting 37 home runs.

trajectory.title: Fourth All-Star selection
trajectory.description: Named to his fourth All-Star Game, continuing his streak of dominant seasons with a .308 batting average and 35 home runs.

name: Vinícius José Paixão de Oliveira Júnior
milestone_by_age_26: Made senior debut for Flamengo at age 16 in 2017, signed with Real Madrid for £38M (national record for a player under 18) at 18, scored the winning goal in the 2022 Champions League final at 21, and was named The Best FIFA Men's Player in 2024 at age 24.
starting_point: Born July 12, 2000 in Sao Goncalo, Brazil; father took him to Flamengo's branch office at age six; joined Flamengo's youth academy and rose through the ranks.
current_position: Forward for Real Madrid and Brazil; named The Best FIFA Men's Player 2024; Ballon d'Or runner-up 2024; one of the world's best footballers.

trajectory.title: Professional debut at Flamengo
trajectory.description: Made his senior debut for Flamengo on May 13, 2017, at age 16, as a substitute in a Brazilian Serie A match.

trajectory.title: Signed for Real Madrid for GBP 38M
trajectory.description: Completed his transfer to Real Madrid for GBP 38 million, a national record for a player under 18, debuting for the club on his 18th birthday.

trajectory.title: Champions League winning goal
trajectory.description: Scored the winning goal in the 2022 Champions League final against Liverpool, cementing his status as a Real Madrid star.

trajectory.title: FIFPRO World 11 inclusion
trajectory.description: Named to the FIFPRO World 11 for the first time, recognizing him among the best players in world football.

trajectory.title: FIFA Men's Player of the Year
trajectory.description: Named The Best FIFA Men's Player and finished runner-up for the Ballon d'Or after scoring the second goal in the 2024 Champions League final and being named the tournament's Player of the Season.

name: Bo Burnham
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest person to record a half-hour Comedy Central special at age 18 in 2008, and released his first hour-long Comedy Central special 'Words Words Words' at age 20 in 2010.
starting_point: Born August 21, 1990 in Hamilton, Massachusetts; raised in a Catholic household; attended St. John's Prep and briefly enrolled at NYU Tisch before pursuing comedy.
current_position: Comedian, filmmaker, and musician; known for Inside (2021) and Eighth Grade (2018); has stepped back from live performing due to anxiety.

trajectory.title: Started YouTube comedy
trajectory.description: Began uploading videos of satirical songs from his bedroom to YouTube, quickly going viral and becoming one of the platform's earliest stars.

trajectory.title: Youngest Comedy Central special
trajectory.description: Became the youngest person to record a half-hour Comedy Central special at age 18, and released his debut EP 'Bo fo Sho.'

trajectory.title: Words Words Words special
trajectory.description: Released his first hour-long Comedy Central special 'Words Words Words' at age 20, establishing himself as a major comedy talent.

trajectory.title: what. special and MTV series
trajectory.description: Released his second special 'what.' on Netflix and co-created and starred in the MTV mockumentary series 'Zach Stone Is Gonna Be Famous.'

trajectory.title: Make Happy and retirement from live performance
trajectory.description: Released 'Make Happy' on Netflix and announced he was stepping away from live performing due to panic attacks on stage.

trajectory.title: Directorial debut with Eighth Grade
trajectory.description: Wrote and directed the critically acclaimed film 'Eighth Grade,' winning the WGA Award and Directors Guild Award for first-time feature directors.

trajectory.title: Inside special and Emmy wins
trajectory.description: Released 'Bo Burnham: Inside' on Netflix, created alone during COVID-19; it won a Peabody Award and three Emmy Awards from six nominations.

name: Pete Davidson
milestone_by_age_26: Joined the cast of Saturday Night Live at age 20 in September 2014, becoming the first SNL cast member born in the 1990s and one of the youngest cast members in the show's history.
starting_point: Born November 16, 1993 on Staten Island, New York; father was a firefighter who died in the 9/11 attacks when Pete was seven; turned to stand-up comedy at age 16.
current_position: Comedian and actor; left SNL in 2022 after eight seasons; starred in The King of Staten Island and Bupkis; continues stand-up and film career.

trajectory.title: First TV appearances
trajectory.description: Made his first onscreen appearance on MTV's Failosophy in February 2013, followed by appearances on Guy Code and Gotham Comedy Live.

trajectory.title: Joined Saturday Night Live
trajectory.description: Joined the cast of SNL at age 20 in September 2014, becoming the first cast member born in the 1990s and one of the youngest cast members ever.

trajectory.title: Trainwreck film role
trajectory.description: Had a small role in Judd Apatow's Trainwreck, which led to Bill Hader recommending him to Lorne Michaels for SNL.

trajectory.title: The King of Staten Island
trajectory.description: Starred in and co-wrote The King of Staten Island, a semi-autobiographical film directed by Judd Apatow.

trajectory.title: Departed SNL
trajectory.description: Left Saturday Night Live after eight seasons in May 2022, transitioning to a full-time film and stand-up career.

trajectory.title: Bupkis series
trajectory.description: Created and starred in Bupkis, a comedy series for Peacock, and voiced Mirage in Transformers: Rise of the Beasts.

name: Jude Bellingham
milestone_by_age_26: Won the UEFA Champions League and La Liga title with Real Madrid in 2024 at age 21, and was voted La Liga Player of the Season.
starting_point: Born June 29, 2003 in Stourbridge, England; father was a sergeant in West Midlands Police and prolific non-league footballer; joined Birmingham City as an under-8.
current_position: Midfielder for Real Madrid and England; one of the best players in the world; 3x FIFPRO World 11; Ballon d'Or third place 2024.

trajectory.title: Birmingham City debut
trajectory.description: Became Birmingham City's youngest first-team player at 16 years and 38 days old in August 2019, and played regularly throughout the 2019-20 season.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Borussia Dortmund
trajectory.description: Joined Borussia Dortmund for a world-record fee for a 17-year-old, and became the club's youngest goalscorer in his first appearance.

trajectory.title: DFB-Pokal winner
trajectory.description: Won the 2020-21 DFB-Pokal with Dortmund, scoring in the final, and established himself as a regular starter in the Bundesliga.

trajectory.title: Signed for Real Madrid for EUR 103M
trajectory.description: Transferred to Real Madrid for EUR 103 million, won the Golden Boy and Kopa Trophy, and was named Bundesliga Player of the Season for 2022-23.

trajectory.title: Champions League and La Liga double
trajectory.description: Won the Champions League and La Liga with Real Madrid in his first season, was voted La Liga Player of the Season, and finished third in the Ballon d'Or.

name: Lamine Yamal
milestone_by_age_26: Won UEFA Euro 2024 with Spain at age 17, becoming the youngest player to score in the tournament's history and winning the Young Player Award; also won the Kopa Trophy as best young player in the world.
starting_point: Born July 13, 2007 in Esplugues de Llobregat, Spain; raised in Rocafonda, a deprived area of Catalonia; son of a mother from Equatorial Guinea and a father from Morocco; scouted by Barcelona at age six.
current_position: Forward for Barcelona and Spain; Kopa Trophy winner 2024 and 2025; Ballon d'Or runner-up 2025; FIFA World Cup winner 2026; one of the world's best young players.

trajectory.title: Joined La Masia
trajectory.description: Scouted by Barcelona at age six and signed for the club in 2014, moving to La Masia academy and racing through age categories faster than any peer.

trajectory.title: Barcelona first-team debut
trajectory.description: Made his first-team debut on April 29, 2023 at 15 years and 290 days, becoming the youngest player to appear for Barcelona's first team in over a century.

trajectory.title: Spain debut and youngest scorer
trajectory.description: Became the youngest player to represent and score for Spain at age 16, and became the youngest player to start a La Liga game since 1939.

trajectory.title: Euro 2024 champion and Young Player Award
trajectory.description: Helped Spain win UEFA Euro 2024, becoming the youngest player to score in the tournament's history and winning the Young Player of the Tournament award.

trajectory.title: Kopa Trophy winner
trajectory.description: Won the Kopa Trophy as the best young player in the world at the Ballon d'Or gala, and was the youngest player ever nominated for the Ballon d'Or.

trajectory.title: Domestic treble and Ballon d'Or runner-up
trajectory.description: Helped Barcelona win a domestic treble under Hansi Flick, scoring 18 goals with 21 assists, and finished as runner-up for the 2025 Ballon d'Or.

trajectory.title: FIFA World Cup winner
trajectory.description: Won his first FIFA World Cup as Spain claimed their second title, with Yamal named La Liga Player of the Season for 2025-26.

name: Anthony Edwards
milestone_by_age_26: Selected 1st overall in the 2020 NBA Draft at 19, became a 4x NBA All-Star by age 24 (2023-2026), and won Olympic gold with Team USA at the 2024 Paris Olympics at 23.
starting_point: Born August 5, 2001 in Atlanta, Georgia; played high school basketball at Holy Spirit Prep; was the #1 recruit in the 2019 class; played one year at University of Georgia.
current_position: Shooting guard for the Minnesota Timberwolves; 4x NBA All-Star; 2x All-NBA Second Team; Olympic gold medalist; one of the NBA's biggest young stars.

trajectory.title: Top recruit and college season at Georgia
trajectory.description: Was the #1 recruit in the 2019 class by 247Sports and played one season at the University of Georgia, averaging 19.1 points per game.

trajectory.title: 1st overall NBA Draft pick
trajectory.description: Selected with the first overall pick by the Minnesota Timberwolves in the 2020 NBA Draft and made his NBA debut on December 23, 2020.

trajectory.title: First NBA All-Star
trajectory.description: Named an NBA All-Star for the first time in the 2022-23 season, averaging 24.6 points per game and leading the Timberwolves to the playoffs.

trajectory.title: Olympic gold and All-NBA
trajectory.description: Won Olympic gold with Team USA at the 2024 Paris Olympics and was named All-NBA Second Team after averaging 25.9 points.

trajectory.title: All-Star and career-best season
trajectory.description: Named to his fourth All-Star Game and averaged a career-best 27.6 points in the 2024-25 season, establishing himself as an MVP candidate.

name: LaMelo Ball
milestone_by_age_26: Named NBA Rookie of the Year in 2021 at 19 and became an NBA All-Star in 2022 at age 20, the fourth-youngest All-Star in NBA history.
starting_point: Born August 22, 2001 in Anaheim, California; son of LaVar Ball; played high school basketball at Chino Hills; played professionally in Lithuania and Australia before the NBA.
current_position: Point guard for the Minnesota Timberwolves (traded from Charlotte Hornets in 2025); NBA All-Star; NBA Rookie of the Year.

trajectory.title: High school state championship
trajectory.description: Won a state championship at Chino Hills High School as a freshman, achieving national prominence alongside his brother Lonzo.

trajectory.title: Professional stint in Lithuania
trajectory.description: Left Chino Hills to sign with Lithuanian professional team Prienai, and later played in the JBA, a league created by his father.

trajectory.title: NBL Next Stars in Australia
trajectory.description: Signed with the Illawarra Hawks of the Australian NBL through the Next Stars program, where his meteoric rise improved his draft stock from second-round to lottery pick.

trajectory.title: 3rd overall NBA Draft pick
trajectory.description: Selected with the third overall pick by the Charlotte Hornets in the 2020 NBA Draft, and made his debut on December 23, 2020.

trajectory.title: NBA Rookie of the Year
trajectory.description: Named NBA Rookie of the Year after averaging 15.7 points, 5.9 rebounds, and 6.1 assists, becoming the youngest player to record a triple-double.

trajectory.title: NBA All-Star
trajectory.description: Named an NBA All-Star in his second season at age 20, the fourth-youngest All-Star in NBA history, averaging 20.1 points and 7.6 assists.

trajectory.title: Traded to Timberwolves
trajectory.description: Traded from the Charlotte Hornets to the Minnesota Timberwolves in a shocking mid-season deal, ending his five-year tenure in Charlotte.

name: Pedri
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Golden Boy and Kopa Trophy in 2021 at age 18 as the world's best young player, having debuted for Barcelona at 17 and been named Best Young Player at Euro 2020.
starting_point: Born November 25, 2002 in Tegueste, Tenerife, Canary Islands; began his career at local club Tegueste before joining Las Palmas youth system.
current_position: Midfielder for Barcelona and Spain; Golden Boy and Kopa Trophy winner; one of the best midfielders in the world; integral to Barcelona's domestic treble in 2024-25.

trajectory.title: Professional debut at Las Palmas
trajectory.description: Promoted to Las Palmas's first team in August 2019 at age 16, becoming the most used player across the season with 34 appearances in Segunda Division.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Barcelona
trajectory.description: Joined Barcelona for EUR 5 million from Las Palmas, making his debut on September 27, 2020, and scoring his first Champions League goal in October.

trajectory.title: Golden Boy and Kopa Trophy
trajectory.description: Won both the Golden Boy and Kopa Trophy as the best young player in the world after playing 52 games in his debut Barcelona season and being named Euro 2020 Young Player of the Tournament.

trajectory.title: La Liga title with Barcelona
trajectory.description: Won his first La Liga title with Barcelona in the 2022-23 season, scoring six goals and establishing himself as a midfield cornerstone.

trajectory.title: Euro 2024 champion with Spain
trajectory.description: Was part of Spain's victorious Euro 2024 campaign despite picking up an injury in the quarter-final win over Germany.

trajectory.title: Domestic treble with Barcelona
trajectory.description: Was integral to Barcelona winning a domestic treble (La Liga, Copa del Rey, Supercopa de Espana) under Hansi Flick, missing just one match all season.

name: Gavi
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Golden Boy and Kopa Trophy in 2022 at age 18 as the world's best young player, having debuted for Barcelona at 17 and become Spain's youngest-ever player.
starting_point: Born August 5, 2004 in Los Palacios y Villafranca, near Seville, Spain; started at local club La Liara before joining Real Betis youth academy, then signed for Barcelona at age 11.
current_position: Central midfielder for Barcelona and Spain; Kopa Trophy winner 2022; returned from knee injury in 2024; continues to be a key player for Barcelona.

trajectory.title: Joined Barcelona's La Masia
trajectory.description: Signed for Barcelona's La Masia academy at age 11 from Real Betis, where he had scored 95 goals for the youth team.

trajectory.title: Barcelona first-team debut
trajectory.description: Made his La Liga debut for Barcelona at 17 years and 24 days old on August 29, 2021, under manager Ronald Koeman, immediately looking like a veteran.

trajectory.title: Youngest Spain international
trajectory.description: Became the youngest player to win a senior international cap for Spain at 17 years and 62 days, starting in a UEFA Nations League semi-final.

trajectory.title: Kopa Trophy and Golden Boy
trajectory.description: Won the Kopa Trophy as the world's best player under 21 at the Ballon d'Or ceremony and the Golden Boy award, after a breakthrough 2021-22 season.

trajectory.title: La Liga and Supercopa winner
trajectory.description: Won La Liga and the Supercopa de Espana with Barcelona, scoring in the Supercopa final against Real Madrid and being named man of the match.

trajectory.title: Serious knee injury
trajectory.description: Suffered a serious knee ligament rupture while on international duty in November 2023, missing nearly the entire 2023-24 season.

trajectory.title: Return and Euro 2024 champion
trajectory.description: Returned from injury in October 2024 and was part of Spain's Euro 2024 winning squad, making 42 appearances across the season.

name: Florian Wirtz
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 2023-24 Bundesliga title with Bayer Leverkusen in an unbeaten season and was named Bundesliga Player of the Season at age 21, after debuting in the Bundesliga at 17 as the league's youngest-ever goalscorer.
starting_point: Born May 3, 2003 in Pulheim, Germany; father Hans-Joachim was a youth academy director; joined 1. FC Koln's academy in 2010 and spent nine years there before moving to Bayer Leverkusen.
current_position: Attacking midfielder for Liverpool and Germany; Bundesliga Player of the Season 2023-24; transferred to Liverpool for a record fee in 2025; one of the best young midfielders in the world.

trajectory.title: Debut at Bayer Leverkusen
trajectory.description: Joined Bayer Leverkusen from 1. FC Koln in January 2020 and made his first team debut at 17, becoming the youngest scorer in Bundesliga history.

trajectory.title: Germany senior debut and U21 Euro champion
trajectory.description: Made his senior Germany national team debut and won the U21 European Championship, establishing himself as one of Germany's top talents.

trajectory.title: ACL injury
trajectory.description: Suffered a torn ACL in March 2022, sidelining him for several months during a critical development period.

trajectory.title: Bundesliga unbeaten double and Player of the Season
trajectory.description: Played a pivotal role in Leverkusen's historic unbeaten Bundesliga and DFB-Pokal double, scoring 18 goals in 49 appearances and being named Bundesliga Player of the Season.

trajectory.title: Record transfer to Liverpool
trajectory.description: Transferred to Liverpool for a club-record fee of approximately GBP 100 million plus bonuses, breaking the Premier League transfer record.

trajectory.title: Key player at Liverpool
trajectory.description: Grew into a key player at Liverpool, contributing six goals and nine assists in all competitions and preparing to lead Germany at the 2026 World Cup.

name: Bukayo Saka
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for Arsenal's first team at 17 in November 2018, became an England international at 19, and was named Arsenal Player of the Year in consecutive seasons (2020-21, 2021-22) while reaching the Euro 2020 final with England.
starting_point: Born September 5, 2001 in Ealing, London; joined Arsenal's Hale End academy at age seven; previously played for Watford's youth teams.
current_position: Right winger for Arsenal and England; one of the Premier League's best players; Arsenal's all-time leading scorer for the England national team.

trajectory.title: Arsenal first-team debut
trajectory.description: Made his first-team debut for Arsenal on November 29, 2018, in a Europa League match, becoming the first player born in 2001 to play in the Premier League.

trajectory.title: England debut and Euro 2020 final
trajectory.description: Made his England senior debut in October 2020 and was part of the England squad that reached the Euro 2020 final, experiencing penalty heartbreak in the final.

trajectory.title: Arsenal Player of the Year
trajectory.description: Named Arsenal Player of the Season for 2020-21, becoming one of the club's most influential players under Mikel Arteta.

trajectory.title: World Cup and second Player of the Year
trajectory.description: Scored three goals at the 2022 Qatar World Cup and was named Arsenal Player of the Season for the second consecutive year.

trajectory.title: Career-best season and Euro 2024
trajectory.description: Finished as Arsenal's top scorer with 20 goals in all competitions and represented England at Euro 2024, becoming Arsenal's all-time leading scorer for England.

trajectory.title: Champions League heroics
trajectory.description: Returned from a hamstring injury to score against Real Madrid in the Champions League, helping Arsenal reach the semi-finals.

name: Phil Foden
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Premier League title with Manchester City in 2018 at age 18, having debuted for the club at 17 and won the FIFA U-17 World Cup Golden Ball in 2017.
starting_point: Born May 28, 2000 in Stockport, Greater Manchester; boyhood Manchester City supporter; joined City's academy at age eight; tuition at St Bede's College paid by the club.
current_position: Midfielder for Manchester City and England; 6x Premier League champion; Premier League Player of the Season 2023-24; PFA Players' Player of the Year 2023-24.

trajectory.title: FIFA U-17 World Cup Golden Ball
trajectory.description: Won the Golden Ball as best player at the FIFA U-17 World Cup in India, scoring twice in the 5-2 final win over Spain and being named man of the match.

trajectory.title: Manchester City debut
trajectory.description: Made his Manchester City debut in November 2017 in a Champions League match against Feyenoord, becoming the fourth-youngest English player to appear in the competition.

trajectory.title: Youngest English Champions League starter
trajectory.description: Became the youngest English player to start a Champions League match at 17 years and 192 days, and won his first Premier League title with City.

trajectory.title: England debut and Premier League champion
trajectory.description: Made his England senior debut in September 2020 and won his third Premier League title with Manchester City in 2020-21.

trajectory.title: Treble with Manchester City
trajectory.description: Won the treble (Premier League, FA Cup, Champions League) with Manchester City in 2022-23, the first English club to achieve this since 1999.

trajectory.title: Premier League Player of the Season
trajectory.description: Named Premier League Player of the Season and PFA Players' Player of the Year after scoring 19 league goals and winning his sixth Premier League title.

name: Eduardo Camavinga
milestone_by_age_26: Won the UEFA Champions League with Real Madrid in 2022 at age 19, having debuted for Rennes at 16 and transferred to Real Madrid for €31m at 18.
starting_point: Born November 10, 2002 in a refugee camp in Cabinda, Angola to Congolese parents; family moved to France when he was young; joined Rennes youth academy in 2013.
current_position: Central midfielder for Real Madrid and France; 2x Champions League winner; World Cup runner-up 2022; one of the most versatile midfielders in world football.

trajectory.title: Rennes senior debut
trajectory.description: Made his senior debut for Stade Rennais at age 16, quickly establishing himself as a regular first-team player in Ligue 1.

trajectory.title: France's youngest debutant in a century
trajectory.description: Made his senior France national team debut at 17, becoming the nation's youngest debutant in over a century.

trajectory.title: Transferred to Real Madrid
trajectory.description: Signed for Real Madrid for EUR 31 million in August 2021, joining one of the world's biggest clubs as a teenager.

trajectory.title: Champions League winner
trajectory.description: Won the UEFA Champions League with Real Madrid in his first season, and was part of the France squad that finished as World Cup runners-up in Qatar.

trajectory.title: Second Champions League and La Liga double
trajectory.description: Won his second Champions League and La Liga double with Real Madrid, cementing his place as a key player in the squad.

name: Jamal Musiala
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Bundesliga debut for Bayern Munich at 17 and won the 2019-20 UEFA Champions League as a squad member, later winning multiple Bundesliga titles and becoming Bayern's youngest-ever goalscorer.
starting_point: Born February 26, 2003 in Stuttgart, Germany; father is British-Nigerian, mother is German with Polish roots; moved to England at age seven; joined Chelsea's academy at age eight.
current_position: Attacking midfielder for Bayern Munich and Germany; one of the best attacking midfielders in the world; German Footballer of the Year 2022; Euro 2024 All-Star.

trajectory.title: Joined Bayern Munich from Chelsea
trajectory.description: Left Chelsea's academy at 16 to join Bayern Munich in July 2019, a controversial move that would prove transformative for his career.

trajectory.title: Bundesliga debut and Champions League squad
trajectory.description: Made his Bundesliga debut on June 20, 2020, becoming Bayern's youngest Bundesliga player at 17 years and 115 days, and was part of the squad that won the 2019-20 Champions League.

trajectory.title: Germany senior debut and first goals
trajectory.description: Chose to represent Germany over England, making his senior Germany debut in March 2021 and scoring his first Bundesliga goals as a regular starter.

trajectory.title: German Footballer of the Year
trajectory.description: Named German Footballer of the Year at age 19 after a breakout season, becoming Bayern's youngest-ever goalscorer in the Bundesliga and Champions League.

trajectory.title: Euro 2024 All-Star and 100 Bundesliga appearances
trajectory.description: Named to the Euro 2024 All-Star Team and became the youngest Bayern Munich player to reach 100 Bundesliga appearances at age 20.

trajectory.title: Contract extension and continued dominance
trajectory.description: Signed a long-term contract extension with Bayern Munich until 2030, solidifying his status as one of the club's most important players.
